title: Swapping input and coin averages of the failure probability
statement:
Suppose $X\times Y$ is a finite probability space, whose probability measure we write $\mathbb{P}$, let $m\in\bbn$, and let $p$ be a public-coin protocol whose shared randomness is a coin tape in $\mathrm{CoinTape}(m)$, with Alice's private input drawn from $X$, Bob's from $Y$, and outputs in $\alpha$. Write $\mathrm{vol}$ for the measure on $\mathrm{CoinTape}(m)$, and for a coin tape $\omega$ and inputs $x,y$ let $\mathrm{rrun}(p,x,y,\omega)$ be the randomized execution of $p$. Then for every function $f\colon X\times Y\to\alpha$,
\[
\int_{\mathrm{CoinTape}(m)} \mathbb{P}\!\left(\bigl\{(x,y)\in X\times Y : \mathrm{rrun}(p,x,y,\omega)\neq f(x,y)\bigr\}\right)\,d\omega
=
\int_{X\times Y} \mathrm{vol}\!\left(\bigl\{\omega\in\mathrm{CoinTape}(m) : \mathrm{rrun}(p,x,y,\omega)\neq f(x,y)\bigr\}\right)\,d\mathbb{P}(x,y).
\]
On the left one first measures, for each fixed coin tape $\omega$, the $\mathbb{P}$-probability of the inputs on which $p$ disagrees with $f$, and then averages over $\omega$; on the right one first measures, for each fixed input pair $(x,y)$, the set of coin tapes on which $p$ disagrees with $f$, and then averages over the inputs.
hypotheses_covered: X × Y is a finite probability space (probability measure P)
m is a natural number (coin tape length)
p is a public-coin protocol over CoinTape(m), X, Y, α
f : X × Y → α is an arbitrary reference function
replaced:
Let $\mu$ be a finite probability space on $X \times Y$, let $m \in \mathbb{N}$, and let
$p$ be a public-coin protocol with coin tape of length $m$.  For any $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$,
\[
  \int_{\omega}\,\mu\!\left(\bigl\{(x,y) \mid p.\mathrm{rrun}(x,y,\omega) \ne f(x,y)\bigr\}\right)\,d\omega
  \;=\;
  \int_{(x,y)}\,\mathrm{vol}\!\left(\bigl\{\omega : \mathrm{CoinTape}\,m \mid
    p.\mathrm{rrun}(x,y,\omega) \ne f(x,y)\bigr\}\right)\,d\mu,
\]
obtained by swapping the order of integration via Fubini's theorem applied to the
failure-indicator function.
